name: Hatched Empire Map
what: The base map for the whole history: a grey-black satellite relief, graded to warm sepia land and near-black seas, with a heavy vignette and film grain. Each power's territory is filled with a diagonal hatch in its own colour (Russia oxblood red, Iran orange, Britain slate blue, yellow for the ancient 'SUPER POWER'). Territories fade or grow in under a soft edge glow. A single country can be introduced as a glowing pale outline with a small white serif name (IRAN, 0:02 / 0:48). Engraved serif sea names ('Black Sea', 'Caspian Sea') sit on the water, and the camera keeps drifting or pushing slowly. One cut is covered by a warm light-leak flare washing across the map (1:06).
job: It shows who controls what in one glance, and the same palette stays on every scene, so the viewer learns that red means Russia and blue means Britain without being told again.
build: AE (or HTML/SVG rendered with alpha): desaturated relief basemap graded sepia, seas crushed to near-black, plus vignette and grain. Country shapes come from GeoJSON as shape layers, filled with a 45-degree stripe pattern (Venetian Blinds, or a tiled stripe PNG at about 50% opacity) in faction colours, with a 1–2 px outline and Glow. Animate fill opacity and a mask-feather grow. Outline reveal: Trim Paths on the stroke plus Glow. Add a slow 2.5D camera push of 3–5% per shot. Premiere just places the rendered plates.
fit: CH1 2020 Pittsburgh and 2a Prague (glowing outline of the city or country with a small serif name, as a place-establisher before the footage). 0d Olympia announcement (glowing outline of Las Vegas). Use it only where a place matters; the rest of the doc is face-led.

name: Octagon Power Badges
what: Every actor in the story is an octagonal token with a thick white rim and a drop shadow, pinned to the map. Nations show a flag, people show a portrait or crowd photo on a flag backdrop (the Shah's plume breaks out above the frame), and companies show an icon. Under each badge sits a black label box with white condensed caps (RUSSIAN EMPIRE, QAJAR IRAN, IRANIAN PEOPLE). The badges scale up when they are the subject, and a badge that is out of play fades to a ghosted, translucent red (Ottoman Empire, 2:08). A badge can change identity on screen: KING becomes SHAH (8:24 to 8:26), IRAN becomes QAJAR IRAN (1:34), and IRANIAN PEOPLE becomes IRANIAN PARLIAMENT (9:28 to 9:30). During that change the octagon turns into a dashed outline while the photo swaps and the label letters scramble before they resolve.
job: It turns a complicated cast into a small set of game pieces the viewer can track. A label change marks a change in status without needing a new graphic.
build: AE precomp per badge: octagon shape layer (8-sided polystar) with a white stroke (about 8% of the diameter) and a drop shadow. Flag, portrait or icon goes in a track-matte layer, and the portrait head is cut out and duplicated above the matte so it breaks the frame. The label is a black rectangle with a white condensed sans (Oswald/Bebas class), tracked +20. Pop on with scale 0 to 105 to 100% over 8 frames. Rename: a Text Animator with Character Offset randomize for about 12 frames, while the rim switches to a dashed stroke and the photo crossfades. Ghosting: 35% opacity plus a red tint. Can be made into a MOGRT with a photo slot and a label field.
fit: CH1 (badge NICK WALKER and badge MARTIN FITZWATER; 'AMATEUR' scrambles to 'IFBB PRO' as both turn pro). CH4 sponsors as logo badges that ghost out one by one as they drop him. 5d Nick's badge label scrambles to 'MR. OLYMPIA'. It gives the rivalry two fixed tokens to return to.

Add a radial gradient (Ramp or CC Light Burst) in the side's colour at 30–40% Add, scattered pulsing dots (a Repeater with wiggle opacity), and Particular or a CC Particle field for the arcs. name: Torn Treaty Card

Animate scale and position for the push-in over about 1 s (ease out). Text in a serif (Cormorant/Libre Caslon class): heading italic, terms in regular weight. Typewriter-reveal each term (Text Animator opacity by character). Bullets are 4 px dots with Glow. Scroll the text group up as lines are added. build: Background: a concrete texture plate with a slight vignette. Cutouts: bg-removed PNGs with a white Stroke (12-16 px) + drop shadow. Highlight: a second, blue stroke, then a 3D Y-rotation and a scale-up. Dashed arcs: shape paths with dashes + Trim Paths. Torn photo: a torn-paper matte PNG with a fold flap.
fit: CH2 2024-25 results run: each show as a sticker (placing badge or contest poster) hopping along dashed arcs, with Nick's and Martin's paths in their two colours until the lines cross at the 2025 Olympia. CH1 2020 Pittsburgh: a lineup of competitor cards with the two men picked out in outline.

name: Cloud-Break Map
what: Google Earth descents start in the clouds and land on an aerial of the town with heavily blurred, tilt-shift edges. A glowing white boundary traces the town limits with a small rotated label, then the name fills the frame in big semi-transparent caps (0:06-0:10). The signature beat splits the aerial along the river into a red-washed half with a white Puma cat and a blue-washed half with the Adidas mark: the town itself was divided (0:44-0:46). Variants: a stylised orange-on-black 3D city map with shirt-icon pins joined by blue dashed routes, a typed-on label and drifting clouds framing it (1:56-2:02); and an aged parchment world map with a shoe icon over Germany radiating white dotted export lines (7:34-7:38).
job: Grounds each chapter in a real place and turns the geography into the argument: one town, two sides; a local trade that reaches a continent.
build: Google Earth Studio for the cloud dive and the tilt. Boundary: an OSM outline as a shape path with Glow. Colour halves: two feathered masks (~40 px) along the river with Tint + Overlay in each side's colour. Logos are white PNGs scaling up with a slight overshoot. Edge blur: Camera Lens Blur through an inverted ellipse. Parchment map: a map illustration + dashed shape lines radiating from the centre with Trim Paths.
fit: CH1 2020 Pittsburgh amateur show (cloud dive + boundary + giant city name). CH2 2a Prague. CH3 the Arnold's host city. CH5 the Olympia in Las Vegas. CH4: the radiating dotted lines can show the pile-on spreading outward.

name: Red Silhouette Set
what: Events nobody filmed are rebuilt as a minimal line-drawing set: the plane cabin, seats, windows and aisle are thin white/grey outlines (about 1-2 px) on a charcoal ground (#1a1a1a to #1f1f1f), with a soft vignette and an edge blur that reads like shallow depth of field. People are flat, featureless silhouettes. Background people are white or mid-grey, and the ONE person the narration is about is solid coral red (#F84040). The red moves with the story: at 1:32 Cooper is red, at 1:34 he turns white, and at 1:36 the stewardess Florence Schaffner turns red and gets a name tag. The camera drifts slowly through the set, and there are POV variants: an over-the-shoulder grey head looking down the aisle at a red figure (4:24), and a red figure striding into frame (4:32). The cold open uses the same language: a red falling figure over a grey point-cloud ground (0:26) dropping into a forest of layered grey pine silhouettes (0:42).
job: It reconstructs a moment that has no footage without pretending to be footage, and the red tells the viewer exactly whom to watch while everything else stays as context.
build: Illustrator line art (white strokes at 40-70% opacity) imported into After Effects as 3D layers. A slow camera dolly with Depth of Field on, plus a vignette. People are photo references rotoscoped (Roto Brush or pen masks) and filled flat with Fill effect colours #F2F2F2, #9A9A9A or #F84040. Red hand-offs are 6-8 frame colour crossfades on the Fill. HTML alternative: inline SVG paths for the set and SVG silhouettes with a CSS fill transition.
fit: 3d (alleged backstage shove): no footage exists, so rebuild a schematic backstage corridor with Martin red and Nick white, captioned ALLEGED, and nothing implied beyond the reports. 3a (handshake skipped): two silhouettes on a line-art stage, one hand held out, with red passing from Nick to Martin as he walks past. 2a (Prague phone hit): a journalist silhouette and a phone in red.

name: Red Isolate Photo
what: A real archival photo (a 1970s aerial of downtown Seattle) is shown first in its own colour (8:28). It then drains to near black-and-white with a soft blur and vignette, while one building, the Seattle-First National Bank, stays sharp and is masked in a translucent deep red (#602829 over the photo, with a brighter red outline) and labelled in small white spaced caps placed on the building (8:30-8:32). The line-art plane diagrams use the same rule: only the part under discussion turns solid red, such as the flaps (3:26), the aft stairs lowering (3:34) and the landing gear (3:22).
job: It points at one thing inside a busy real image. The rest of the frame is kept as proof and context, while the eye is told 'this one'. It extends the film's single-accent colour code to photographs and diagrams.
build: Premiere: two copies of the photo. The bottom copy gets Lumetri Saturation 0 to 10, a slight Gaussian blur and a vignette. The top copy gets a pen mask around the subject (Roto Brush in After Effects for a person) plus a Fill or Tint in red at Multiply/Color blend, about 60-70%, and a thin red stroke on the mask edge. Keyframe saturation 100 to 0 over about 1 s, then the mask fill fades in over 8 frames, then the label. HTML: CSS filter grayscale() on the base, with an SVG clipPath copy of the subject using mix-blend-mode: multiply.
fit: 0a: the freeze on Martin cheering at the Arnold awards. The stage drains to grey, Martin alone goes red, and a Pointer Tag names him. 3c (the cheer): the same shot again, so the cold open pays off. 5d: the Olympia crowning still with Nick isolated, held through the 8 s of silence.

name: Pointer Tag
what: This is the film's single label system for both people and places. It is a small black rectangle with a crisp white border of about 2 px, a small triangular pointer under its centre, and white condensed letter-spaced uppercase text: FLORENCE SCHAFFNER, TINA MUCKLOW, DAN COOPER, SEATTLE, WA, PORTLAND, OR. On a 3D set it is tilted to match the scene's perspective and sits directly over the person's head. It builds in two beats: the empty box pops on first (2:14), then the name fills in (2:16). In map scenes the same tag stands on a short white stem above the location.
job: It names whoever or whatever just entered the story, at the point of interest, without a lower third. Because the same mark is used everywhere, the viewer learns it once and reads it instantly.
build: A MOGRT: a shape layer (black fill, 2 px white stroke, triangle pointer) with a text layer in a condensed sans such as DIN Condensed or Bebas Neue at tracking +100 to 150. Animate the box width 0 to 100% over 4-6 frames with an overshoot ease, then reveal the text with a mask wipe or typewriter. In After Effects make it 3D and parent it to the subject's null so it inherits the camera move. HTML: a div with border plus a ::after triangle, animated with GSAP.
fit: The first appearance of every named face: 0b the YouTuber, 0c Martin at the presser, the CH2 coach, the CH4 head judge, Phil Heath / Andrew Jacked / Iain Valliere before their quote cards, the best friend (Card 4), 5g Nick. Also place tags on CH1 Pittsburgh and 2a Prague.

name: Red Dash Map
what: A dark, desaturated relief map: charcoal land (#252525) with faint hillshade and a fine grey road network, slate-blue water (#3b454f) and a heavy vignette. A Pointer Tag pins the origin (SEATTLE, WA). A thin red dashed line then draws itself across the map along an arc, and the destination tag pops on at its end (MEXICO CITY). Other uses: a red dashed loop for a plane circling the airport, a solid red street route between two tagged places, several white dashed alternative routes fanning out, and a big red dot pin when the camera dives in from a regional to a street scale. For an area, a translucent red band with a dashed centre line and a green-outlined translucent polygon (SEARCH AREA) appear, each labelled with white leader lines and small caps (EARLIEST / LATEST BAILOUT POINT), plus a white dashed measuring line marked 27 KM. Camera moves are a pull-out from local to continental (3:12-3:16) and a push-in to a pin (9:08-9:14).
job: It shows where things happened and how far apart they were, as a journey the viewer can follow. Red is the path of the story, while white or green marks options, possibilities and search zones.
build: A Mapbox Studio custom dark style (or a GEO layer in After Effects), exported as a large still or tiles and moved with an After Effects camera. Routes are shape-layer paths with a dashed red stroke (2-3 px, #F84040) animated with Trim Paths End 0 to 100 over 1-1.5 s, easeInOut. Tags are the Pointer Tag MOGRT. Zones are shape polygons at 25-35% fill with a 2 px outline, revealed with Trim Paths and then the fill fading in. HTML: a static map image plus an SVG path with stroke-dasharray, a mask, and stroke-dashoffset animation.
fit: CH1: a pin on Pittsburgh (2020 amateur show) where both men turn pro. CH2: a red dashed arc out to Prague at 2a, then on to the Arnold. One line per man on the same map is possible, but the 'lines cross' moment belongs to a chart rather than a map.

name: Exhibit Grid
what: Each physical piece of evidence is a real cut-out object (plane ticket, clip-on tie, eight cigarette butts, two parachutes, ransom-note bills) lying on an infinite dark perspective grid floor: thin grey grid lines at low opacity that fade into black at the edges. A white spaced-caps catalogue label lies flat on the floor beside it, rotated to the object's axis: EVIDENCE #4: TWO PARACHUTES. The camera hangs at about 45 degrees and drifts or orbits slightly. Items swap by sliding diagonally along the grid, the old one exiting top-left as the next arrives (5:28-5:32). The first exhibit pushes from the full object into an extreme macro with very shallow depth of field on the key handwriting (DAN COOPER, flight 305, 1:14-1:20).
job: It makes the case feel forensic and countable. Each object is numbered evidence in a running catalogue that the viewer is assembling with the narrator.
build: After Effects 3D: a solid with the Grid effect (1 px lines, about 15% white) rotated X -90 degrees, plus a dark radial vignette. Each object is a cut-out PNG (or a 3D scan or Element 3D) laid on the plane with a soft contact shadow. The label is a 3D text layer laid on the floor. Use a 2-node camera with a 5-10 degree orbit, and Depth of Field on for the macro push. Items slide with Position on the grid diagonal, with motion blur on. HTML: CSS 3D (perspective plus rotateX(60deg) rotateZ(-30deg)) on a container holding a repeating-linear-gradient grid and the object image.
fit: CH3 thesis, Text Cards 1-2: lay the two Instagram posts from that night side by side on the grid as EXHIBIT #1 and EXHIBIT #2, with the camera dollying between them. CH4: the apology post (Card 3) arrives as EXHIBIT #3. 2a: the journalist's phone as an object if a still exists.

name: Inverted Newsprint
what: Period newspaper clippings are shown in negative: light grey type on a charcoal, grainy paper surface, so the press fits the film's dark palette. Each page is tilted steeply in 3D perspective with extreme shallow depth of field, so only the headline is sharp and the body copy melts into blur. The camera pushes in slowly, and as it reaches the key phrase that phrase turns red: $200,000, 'Please Check Your $20 Bills, FBI Asks', $25,000 reward. Long lists (the published ransom serial numbers, 8:34-8:38) get the same tilted, defocused treatment. Moves between clippings are rack-focus swaps (9:28-9:32, one headline blurs out as the next sharpens) or a diagonal wipe to the next shot (8:26).
job: It shows that the press really said this, and makes the one phrase that matters impossible to miss. The page reads as texture and authority while the red reads as the point.
build: Scan the clipping, then Invert + Levels (paper to about #1e1e1e, ink to about #cfcfcf) plus a paper-grain overlay. In After Effects, a 3D layer rotated about 20-35 degrees on X/Y, a camera with Depth of Field (large aperture, focus distance on the headline) and a slow push-in. The red is a duplicate layer masked to the headline words with Fill #E84048, faded in over 6 frames. Transitions are a Camera Lens Blur ramp between clippings, or a Linear Wipe at about -30 degrees. HTML: CSS 3D transform plus filter: invert(1) blur(), with a sharp masked copy of the headline.
fit: CH4: sponsors drop him, and the internet piles on, as a run of inverted, tilted headlines and articles with the sponsor or verdict word in red. 5d: the Olympia results list as a tilted, defocused list that pushes in until '12. Martin Fitzwater' racks into focus and turns red.

name: Red Word Quote
what: A verbatim quote fills the frame over the previous scene, which is frozen, darkened by about 80% and blurred (red silhouettes or a map still ghost through). Transcript excerpts are set in bold white condensed spaced uppercase, left-aligned, with quote marks and editorial [BRACKETS]. Beneath, a small italic caps attribution line: EXCERPT FROM AN INTERVIEW WITH COPILOT WILLIAM RATACZAK. As the narrator reads, key phrases light up red one at a time: 5 TO 10 MINUTES, then OSCILLATION, then VIBRATION. A handwritten variant sets the hijacker's demands in a script font, line by line, with key items in red ($200,000, two back parachutes, fuel truck). A note variant shows the handwritten note inside a small card with a rough, deckled double white border on black, where 'bomb' turns red (1:42-1:44).
job: It puts the exact words on screen so the viewer reads the evidence instead of hearing a paraphrase, and the timed red marks the words the argument depends on.
build: Freeze the last frame of the previous shot, then Gaussian Blur 25-40 and Brightness -70 (or a black solid at 80%). Text in Premiere Essential Graphics or HTML: a condensed sans, all caps, tracking +80, line-height 1.6. Lines fade and rise in about 8 px over 10 frames. Each keyword is its own span or text range, and its colour animates white to #F84040 over 3 frames on the spoken word. The attribution is about 40% of body size, italic caps at 60% opacity. Note variant: a rough-edge border PNG frame with a handwriting font.
fit: 0c: Martin's press-conference quote. 1b-1d: the 2022 interview line where he admits the beef. Plant the 'low sleep, a blow-up, a sponsor walking away' line with all three phrases red, then repeat the card at 4a with the same reds as the callback. CH4: the head judge quote, and the Phil Heath / Andrew Jacked / Iain Valliere defences (one card each, attributed). 5a: 'I will win'. Note variant for the short post lines, Card 4 and Card 5.

name: Dossier Readout
what: A spare, police-file description sheet on black. On the left is a column of field names in light grey letter-spaced caps, right-aligned: SEX, RACE, COMPLEXION, AGE, HEIGHT, WEIGHT, BUILD, HAIR, EYES. Against them, the values type in one at a time in bold white condensed caps as the narrator reads them, with metric conversions as tiny superscripts (5'9"-6' (180-183 CM)). Once the sheet is full, flat white cut-out silhouettes of the clothing (overcoat, white shirt, shoes, sunglasses) swap in one after another on the right. The sequence ends on the famous composite sketch in a white-bordered frame.
job: It turns a description into data the viewer can scan, and it builds the subject up attribute by attribute before showing the face.
build: HTML/CSS is the simplest: a two-column grid with labels in #9a9a9a at tracking +200 and values in white bold condensed type, revealed with a per-row clip-path wipe or typewriter timed to the transcript. Icons are white-filled PNG cut-outs (Photoshop: select subject, fill white) that crossfade with a 4-frame scale from 96 to 100%. Premiere: Essential Graphics text with a Crop-wipe on each value row.
fit: CH1: when both men turn pro in 2020, build a side-by-side readout per man (age, height, stage weight, pro card, best placing) with a posing silhouette on the right, then return to it in CH2 for the 2024-25 results run with updated values. It sets up the rivalry as two comparable files.

name: Float Frame
what: Real archival footage and photos never fill the screen. They sit as a smaller rectangle (about 50-60% of frame width) with a clean off-white border of about 4-6 px, floating on the charcoal background with generous negative space and slight film grain. A tiny black source or date tag sits inside a corner (FBI top-left, 'BEFORE NOV 30, 1971' or '1972' bottom-left on the sketches). Frames enter over the previous graphic while it dims to black (7:42) and leave as a fast horizontal slide with heavy motion blur (4:52, 6:08). Successive versions of one image (the composite sketch evolving from B&W to colour) replace each other in a frame that shifts scale and position.
job: It separates documentary proof from the animated reconstruction. The border says 'this is the real record' and the source tag credits it, so the illustrated world and the archive never blur together.
build: Premiere: scale the clip to 55%, add a white Stroke via a Graphics rectangle layer behind it (or the Edge effect in After Effects), plus a grain overlay, and a small Essential Graphics tag in the corner. Push the scale 100 to 104% over the hold. For the exit, Transform effect Position keyframes off-screen over 6-8 frames with Shutter Angle 180-360 (motion blur), or CC Force Motion Blur in After Effects. HTML: a bordered div with a box-shadow and a GSAP x tween with a motion-blur filter.
fit: Every borrowed clip: 0b and 5e/5f YouTuber commentary (with a corner tag naming the channel), 5g Nick's vlog, CH1 2020 Pittsburgh amateur-show photos (2020 date tag), 2021 results footage. Use the version-swap for a 2020 to 2025 physique progression of each man.

name: Whisper Card
what: Chapter breaks are an almost empty charcoal frame (#111111) with tiny type in the centre: small spaced condensed caps 'CHAPTER 2:' over a handwritten script title, 'The Manhunt Begins', in white, only about 4% of frame height. The script writes on (5:10), holds in silence, then defocuses into a blur and dissolves (5:14) as the next scene fades up through it (at 0:58 the map appears behind the blurring title). A date variant puts a lone bold condensed spaced date, 'NOV 17, 1973', at centre on black, and three dates cut in 2-s succession (9:02-9:06) to compress years before a map pin. The main title uses the same pairing, small caps 'THE SEARCH FOR' above red script 'D. B. Cooper' on a rough dark brush patch over the forest (0:44-0:48).
job: It gives the viewer a breath and a reset between acts. Small type in large black space feels quiet and serious, and the date variant marks a jump in time with no narration.
build: Background #111111. Label: condensed sans, all caps, about 18 px at 1080p, tracking +200, 80% white. Title: a handwriting/script font at about 40 px, revealed with a left-to-right mask (or Trim Paths on a traced path in After Effects). Hold 1.5-2 s, then the exit: Gaussian or Camera Lens Blur 0 to 40 plus opacity 100 to 0 over 12 frames, overlapping the next shot's fade-in. Dates: bold condensed caps, tracking +250, hard cuts every 2 s. HTML: the same, with CSS filter blur() keyframes.
fit: 0d: 'SEPTEMBER 26, 2026' alone on black in the date variant, then the Olympia announcement. The title card 'SAME NIGHT' uses the script-over-small-caps pairing, with the script in red like the D. B. Cooper lockup. CH1-CH5 openers use 'CHAPTER 1:' plus a script title. A date run at the top of CH2 ('2024' / '2025') compresses the results run. The bookend black before 'One of them is.' uses the same type and blur-in.

name: Panel Booth Host
what: The host sits dead centre in a medium close-up from one locked-off camera. The room is dark and warm, with four tall black acoustic-diffuser panels set symmetrically behind him: two frame his head and two sit at the edges. The light is a single low-key warm source, with a heavy vignette and brown/olive tones. The only saturated colour is his green cap, and a mic stem sits bottom-centre. Between jump cuts the frame shifts only a few percent in scale or position, so there are no real punch-ins. He arrives late, first appearing at 3:26 after a cold open that is entirely archive, and after that he mostly shows up in short 2–6 s pops between archive runs. The longest stretch is about 16 s (6:34–6:50). Cuts into and out of him are hard cuts. He shares the frame with footage only once, in the sponsor read: full-frame B&W security-cam footage with the host in a small bottom-right box about 25% of the frame width (4:30–4:56).
job: The host is the narrator who interrupts. Each return to camera lands a verdict or a joke on what the archive just showed, then hands back to the evidence. The dark, symmetrical, vignetted booth makes him feel like a late-night storyteller and keeps him tonally consistent with the gritty archive.
build: Shoot locked off at eye level with the face centred and symmetrical background shapes either side of the head. Grade low-key and warm: lift the shadows slightly towards brown, add a strong elliptical vignette (Lumetri Vignette around -1.5 to -2.0), and leave one saturated accent colour. In Premiere, cut jump-cuts with a 0–5% scale nudge, never a hard punch. For reaction moments, scale the host plate to about 25% and pin it bottom-right (16 px inset, no border) over the full-frame clip.
fit: Host intro after 0d, and every CH1–CH5 host return. Copy the set symmetry, the warm low-key grade and the vignette, not the low screen share, because SAME NIGHT is face-led. Use the corner box for 0b and 5e/5f so the host reacts to the YouTuber clips without leaving the frame.

name: Headline Avalanche
what: In about 25 s of the cold open (0:14–0:38), roughly six different documents fire back to back, each held 2–4 s: a dark-mode earnings headline, three WhatsApp screenshots side by side on a slate-grey backdrop, an ESPN page with a highlighted tax-lien clause, a dark-navy child-support article, a lawsuit article dissolving into a casino photo, and a white 'Denies Rumors' headline that drops away into the 50 Cent radio clip. Dark-mode and light-mode pages alternate, and photos of Floyd with cash sit between them. The full cold open runs archive-only until the host appears at 3:26.
job: Shows that the trouble is real and many-sided before any explanation: too many sources to dismiss. The pile-up builds the 'how did it come to this?' question that the flashback to childhood (1:24) then answers.
build: Capture each article or post as a full-frame screenshot and alternate dark and light ones. Cut on VO phrases at 2–4 s per item. Join them with hard cuts, the occasional cross-dissolve into a photo (0:32), and a Dust Void Drop into the first clip. Give every page a slow 3–5% push-in plus a vignette so each still moves. HTML option: a stack of article components rendered as frames.
fit: CH4 'sponsors drop him' plus 'the internet piles on'. Stack 5–6 headlines, posts and comments in about 20 s, then cut hard to the host or to Phil Heath's quote card. A shorter 3-item version also works in the 0a–0c cold open.

name: Dust Void Drop
what: A single artifact is isolated on an empty field sprinkled with sparse film-dust specks. The field is black with white specks for dark items and off-white with black specks for light ones, and the artifact can be a headline block, a rounded-corner video card about 60% of the frame width, or a fight poster ('THE WORLD AWAITS', 8:00). The artifact travels vertically. It drops in from the top over the outgoing shot (1:00, 0:14), sits centred on the void (1:02, 0:16), then keeps falling out the bottom over the next shot as the background swaps (1:04, 0:38). The motion uses no blur and no rotation.
job: Pulls one piece of evidence out of the noise and makes it the whole frame. The fall-through motion also acts as the transition, so the document carries the viewer from one scene to the next.
build: In After Effects or HTML, use a solid #050505 (or #f2f2f0) plus a sparse dust-speck overlay (a film-dust plate on Screen or Multiply at 30–50%) and a soft vignette. The artifact layer has 10–12 px corner radius and a soft drop shadow. Keyframe position Y from about -60% to 50% (ease-out, ~0.4 s), hold, then 50% to about 160% (ease-in, ~0.4 s). Keep the outgoing and incoming shots underneath for the first and last ~0.4 s. Export with alpha so it can be placed on V3 in Premiere.
fit: 0d: the black card 'SEPTEMBER 26, 2026' dropping through into the Olympia announcement. Text Cards 3–5 (apology post, best friend's post, Martin's line), with each post falling onto the void and then through into the next shot. Text Cards 1–2 could share one void side by side.

name: Read-Along Highlighter
what: A full-frame article screenshot (serif or sans body, real page typography) sits on white with a grey edge vignette, faint dust specks and a slow push-in. The source domain appears bottom-left (espn.com, badlefthook.com). A flat yellow highlighter (#ffff3c-ish, square ends, behind the text) wipes left to right across the exact clause as the VO reads it, line after line, for about 14 s (9:02–9:16), and stops where the narration stops. The page then defocuses and fades out on a heavy blur (9:18). Shorter versions highlight a single phrase ('tax lien of more than $7.2 million', '2.4 million buys').
job: Proof in the source's own words: the viewer reads along with the narrator, so the claim feels quoted, not paraphrased. The final blur releases the page and signals 'that's the point, moving on'.
build: Screenshot the page at 2x. In After Effects, add a yellow shape layer per line on Multiply under the text, with each line's width keyframed linearly to the VO word timings (words.json gives exact times), plus a 3–5% scale push across the shot and a vignette. The exit is Gaussian blur 0→40 with a fade over about 0.6 s. HTML: put spans behind the text with clip-path inset animating per line from the transcript timings.
fit: CH4: the head-judge quote and the apology post (Card 3), with the highlight tracking the narrator. CH1: 'low sleep, a blow-up, a sponsor walking away' if read off an article. Lift 4a ('low sleep') can re-highlight the same line as a callback.

name: Blur-Isolate Row
what: A data table from an article (Date · Opponent · Location · Total Purse) is shown in grey-on-charcoal over a darkened, ghosted photo of the subject that is dissolving away. Everything is heavily Gaussian-blurred except the header row and the one row being spoken: 'Oct 1996 (debut) · Roberto Apodaca · Las Vegas · $2,500'. The blurred rows below still show how long the list is, and the source domain sits bottom-left (givemesport.com).
job: Isolates one data point in its context. The viewer sees there is a long list and exactly which line matters, which here is the tiny first purse that sets up the rise to millions.
build: Screenshot the table. In After Effects, duplicate it: the bottom copy gets Gaussian blur 25–35, and the top copy is masked to the header plus the target row with a 2–4 px feather. Darken the page and composite it over the previous photo at about 30% opacity, then dissolve the photo out. Animate the mask down to the next row to walk a list. Premiere alternative: a blur adjustment layer with an inverted mask.
fit: 5d: the results list zooms to '12. Martin Fitzwater' with every other row blurred, so his placing is the only sharp line. Also the CH1 2021 results and the CH2 2024–25 results run, one row at a time.

name: Tale-of-Tape Strip
what: This is a Wikipedia-style 'Tale of the tape' table: a grey header bar, bold row labels (Boxer / Nickname / Hometown / Purse), blue link-coloured names and two columns, one per fighter. It is used two ways. In the full-frame version (5:54–6:00), the fight footage washes out to white, the card fades up, and the table holds on off-white dusty paper with a vignette and a slow push. In the lower-band version (6:52–7:02), the table is a white rounded card about 55% of the frame width that rises from the bottom edge over a fight photo. The photos change behind it, one per fight (Mitchell, Judah, Castillo...), with horizontal pushes, and the card drops away on the last push.
job: Puts the money and the matchup on screen as cold facts, fight after fight, so the viewer tracks the purse climbing without a chart.
build: Build it as an HTML component (system sans, #eaecf0 header, #3366cc names, 1 px row rules), rendered with alpha per fight. For the lower band, slide Y up from the bottom edge over about 0.4 s and keep it on its own track while photos push underneath. For the full-frame version, cross-fade the footage to white (Lumetri exposure up or a white solid at 80%), then the card, then the paper and dust overlay, with a 3% push.

name: Year Ghost

It is never a clean title card: the numerals are translucent and blended INTO the footage (screen/lighten feel), filled either near-white or the channel's dusty pink/salmon, and they take the same scanlines and slight RGB fringe as the picture. Put it UNDER the global scanline/grain adjustment so it shares the texture. Flicker/fade in over ~12 frames (two quick opacity steps), hold ~1.5 s, fade out, with a slow 100->103% scale. name: Kin Tag
what: A three-line name stack set in the negative space beside a face, right-aligned toward the person: the NAME in bold (white, or the house dusty pink), the ROLE in a light weight below it ('Aerospace engineer', 'Recording engineer'), and the person's RELATION TO THE SUBJECT in parentheses in a smaller light grey ('(Jack's mother)', '(Jack's step-brother)', '(Jack's step-father)'). Two people in one photo each get their own stack (1:56). The lighter variant is a single pink name with a soft glow placed next to an actor's head in film footage ('Tim Robbins', 'John Cusack', 'Kyle Gass'). There is no bar, box or line, only type with a soft shadow.

Pink variant #E9A1A8 with a 20 px soft outer glow. Fade up and rise 8 px over 10 frames, hold for the whole shot, cut out with the shot.

name: Tape Morph

A grinning B&W child with a mop of hair (4:58) dissolves into a warm-sepia buzz-cut teenager staring down the lens (5:02).
